# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-5189 # Review — PAN-5189 ## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — PR #5214's description omits the size, license and Effect evidence that AC-1, AC-14/NFR-5 and AC-parent-10 require ## Context - Run ID: agent-pan-5189-review-146e666a - Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5189/.pan/review/agent-pan-5189-review-146e666a/context.json - Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5189 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5189 - PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5214 - HEAD reviewed: 146e666a8eb040d47e2ac2cb29d139f6476f9dc5 - Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base db8fda7c4b8 (origin/main); no prior review cycle - Spec: .pan/drafts/pan-5189.md (FR-1..FR-12, NFR-1..NFR-5, AC-1..AC-17, AC-parent-10) ## Blocking Findings ### [requirements] PR description lacks the evidence three acceptance criteria require — PR #5214 body - Severity: ! (MUST) - Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (process deliverable); in_pr_scope - Trigger and changed-code connection: spec §5 says "Before `pan done`, the agent copies every `PR-notes:` block on the branch … into the PR description." The blocks were written to commit bodies (deps item: before sizes + license table; router-and-host item: after sizes; sheet-engine, engine-shared, document-pages, office-archive notes) but never copied. The PR body is 27 lines: the checklist plus three screenshots. - Expected / observed / impact: - AC-1 expects the before sizes and the WI-1 license table in the PR description. They are absent. - AC-14 / NFR-5 expect the before and after `du -sm dist/dashboard/public`, `unpackedSize` and packed `size`. They are absent. The numbers matter: the commit notes say packed size goes from 45,966,490 to 121,777,712 bytes (2.6x) and unpacked from 202 MB to 391 MB. The human merging this needs to see that on the PR. - AC-parent-10 expects the D-1 license outcome and D-2 Effect outcome, naming any checkpoint fallback. They are absent. - Evidence: `gh pr view 5214 --json body -q .body | grep -i "unpackedSize\|du -sm\|License sweep"` matches nothing (the only hit for `TaggedErrorClass` is a checklist title). `git log origin/main..HEAD --format=%B` shows the `PR-notes:` blocks. - Fix: edit the PR description and paste in every `PR-notes:` block from `git log origin/main..HEAD --format=%B`. Add one line each for D-1 (all five betteroffice packages accepted; OFL-1.1 font files accepted, no format dropped) and D-2 (`Schema.TaggedError` → `Schema.TaggedErrorClass`, no Schema-block fallback taken), and note that D-3's size fallback was not taken. No code change. ## Non-blocking Findings 1. **~ [correctness] A Mermaid parse error leaves Mermaid's error graphic attached to `document.body`** — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/explorer/viewers/mermaid/MermaidViewer.tsx`, the `mermaid.initialize({…})` call. - Classification: implementation defect, in_pr_scope (new code). - Trigger: open any `.mmd` that passes the lexical guard but fails to parse. `mermaid.render(id, text)` runs with no container, so Mermaid appends `div#d` to `document.body`. On a parse error without `suppressErrorRendering`, it renders its "error" diagram into that div and throws before calling `removeTempElements()`. The viewer shows the binary card as specified, but at least one such div stays in the body after the tab closes. Mermaid removes an element with the same id on its next render, and `useId` values can repeat at the same tree position, so the leak is bounded but real. - Evidence: static read of `node_modules/.bun/mermaid@11.17.2/node_modules/mermaid/dist/mermaid.core.mjs`, the `render` function (lines ~1661–1758): `if (config.suppressErrorRendering) { removeTempElements(); throw … }`, else `fromText("error")`, and `if (C) throw C; return u(), {…}`. Not reproduced in a browser, so whether the stray SVG is visible in the dashboard layout is unverified. The unit test mocks `mermaid`, so it cannot show this. - Fix: add `suppressErrorRendering: true` to the `initialize` options. Mermaid then removes its temporary element and rethrows, and the viewer's existing catch shows the binary card. 2. **~ [correctness] A failed `import('mermaid')` or a throwing `initialize` leaves the viewer on Loading forever** — `MermaidViewer.tsx`, `void import('mermaid').then(async …)`. - The `try/catch` wraps only `mermaid.render`. A chunk-load failure (for example, an open tab after `pan reload` replaces hashed assets) rejects outside it, so FR-10's binary-card fallback is not reached and the rejection is unhandled. Fix: add a `.catch` that sets the `failed` state, or move the `import` and `initialize` inside the `try`. 3. **~ [scope/docs] The ERD fix will be undone by its generator** — `docs/overdeck-db-erd.mmd` (commit 32d3b6d459e). - The file is generated by `scripts/gen-overdeck-erd.py` (`docs/overdeck-db-erd-notes.md`: "Regenerate with: `python3 scripts/gen-overdeck-erd.py`"). The generator still emits `" ".join(flags)` (`PK FK`) and the trailing ` %% logical` comment (line 348). The next regeneration brings back both parse errors. This change is also outside PAN-5189's scope. Fix: make the same change in the generator (`",".join(flags)`, move `%% logical` to its own line or drop it) in this PR or a follow-up. 4. **~ [docs] DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE says notebook HTML outputs use `sandbox=""`; the code uses `sandbox="allow-same-origin"`** — `docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md`, the "Notebooks." bullet of the new tier-2 section. - `DocumentPages.tsx` sets `sandbox={props.output ? 'allow-same-origin' : ''}`, and notebook outputs render with `output`. NFR-3 allows either value and scripts stay blocked, so this is a security non-issue, but the doc is wrong. Fix the sentence to say `allow-same-origin` (no `allow-scripts`). 5. **? [requirements] GFM footnotes survive the inert markdown plugin as in-page links** — `viewers/notebook/NotebookMarkdown.tsx`, `inertNotebookMarkdown`. - The plugin removes `link`, `linkReference`, `definition`, `image`, `imageReference` and `html`, but with `remark-gfm` a `[^x]` footnote produces `footnoteReference`/`footnoteDefinition` nodes, which react-markdown renders as ``. FR-7's wording ("link targets and definitions are removed") is not fully met. Impact is low: the href always starts with `#user-content-fn-`, so it cannot match the dashboard's `#/shared/…` or `#agent=` hash routes, and it fetches nothing. Not reproduced in this session: a render test with `[^x]` and a `[^x]: note` definition would confirm it. Optional fix: also drop `footnoteReference` (or turn it into text) and `footnoteDefinition`. 6. **? [requirements] The timeout text has an extra sentence** — `OpenXmlOfficeViewer.tsx` and `OdfViewer.tsx` say "This document took too long to preview. Open it in another app." FR-5 specifies only the first sentence (upstream text). The test matches the prefix. Cosmetic. 7. **? [requirements] AC-4's literal grep prints one line** — `git grep -n "openEpub\|openRtf" -- src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/explorer` matches the doc comment on line 1 of `office/__tests__/extendedDocumentPreview.test.ts` ("…with openEpub/openRtf/openNotebook dropped"). No code uses either function, so the intent is met; reword the comment if you want the literal check clean. 8. **? [maintainability] `engine/slide-text.ts` script-range regexes now hold literal code points instead of `\uXXXX` escapes** (search `['hebrew', /[`). I checked all 65,536 BMP code points: the four regexes match exactly the same set as upstream. But the source now contains invisible characters such as U+FEFF, which makes the ranges unreadable and fragile under editors. Optional: restore the escapes. 9. **Spec concern (not an implementation defect): install size.** The commit notes report `dist/dashboard/public` 99 MB → 248 MB, packed 46 MB → 122 MB, unpacked 202 MB → 391 MB. D-3 accepted this (no pack-size gate exists; assets load only when an Office file opens), and CI's pack/release-related jobs passed. It belongs in the PR description (blocking finding) so the operator sees it. 10. **Stub UI finding (manifest) — mitigated.** `engine/OfficePages.tsx:149` `const [near, setNear] = useState(false)` has a writer: the IntersectionObserver at line 155 (`([entry]) => setNear(entry?.isIntersecting ?? false)`). Not a stub. ## Coverage ### Changed-file ledger (75 files) | File(s) | Status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | viewers/viewer-router.ts | reviewed | §6.4 exactly: rows 7a/7b/7c after archive, before csv/tsv and text; `officeKindOf`; MERMAID set; header sentence. +18/-4 (NFR-2 ≤25). | | viewers/FileViewer.tsx | reviewed | Four `lazy(() => import(…))` viewers; office/notebook/mermaid cases per §6.4; header lists mermaid + betteroffice. +20/-5. | | viewers/mermaid/MermaidViewer.tsx | reviewed | Guard verbatim, strict init, `` data URL; findings 1, 2. | | viewers/notebook/NotebookMarkdown.tsx, NotebookPreview.tsx, NotebookViewer.tsx, notebookParse.ts | reviewed | Inert plugin + `skipHtml`; `
` code; 8 MiB `readBounded`; 16 iframe bound; data: images only; finding 5. Diffed against upstream. |
| viewers/office/DocumentPages.tsx | reviewed | DOMPurify allow-list, data-image filter, CSP and sandbox unchanged from upstream. |
| viewers/office/OpenXmlOfficeViewer.tsx, OdfViewer.tsx | reviewed | Worker lifecycle, abort, 30 s timer, BinaryCard fallback, native `
